html:
A Korean scholar and philosopher of the Joseon dynasty, known by his pen name Toegye. He is widely held to be Korea's greatest Neo-Confucian thinker.

Yi Hwang passed the state exams and held office, but the court of his day was full of purges of scholars, and he kept withdrawing to his home near Andong. There he founded the academy later called Dosan Seowon and taught many students. He wrote at length on the ideas of Zhu Xi, and his famous debate by letter with the younger scholar Gi Daeseung, on how principle and material force shape human feelings, set the terms of Korean philosophy for centuries.

His followers formed the Yeongnam school, which became one of the main factions at court. His writings were also read in Tokugawa Japan. His portrait is on the South Korean 1000 won note, with Dosan Seowon on the back; Yi I, his younger contemporary, is on the 5000 won note.
sum: A Korean scholar and philosopher of the Joseon dynasty, known by his pen name Toegye. He is widely held to be Korea's greatest Neo-Confucian thinker.
